newsitem.title: INDIA: Indian firm insures elephants - with cremation coverage.
newsitem.headline: Indian firm insures elephants - with cremation coverage.

text.p: An Indian firm has launched a group insurance scheme for elephants, including $700 for cremation expenses, the Press Trust of India said on Tuesday.
The news agency said state-run Oriental Insurance Co unveiled the plan late on Monday in the southern state of Kerala in collaboration with the All Kerala Elephant Owners Association.
Five brightly adorned elephants were the among first to be covered by the scheme.

The scheme's benefits include a payment of 25,000 rupees ($700) towards a domesticated elephant's cremation expenses and 2,500 rupees for the cost of administering tranquillisers in case the animal runs amok.
The premium is just three rupees per 1,000 rupees of insurance, the news agency said.
Elephants are widely found in Kerala's dense tropical forests and serve as proud mascots in numerous Hindu temples that dot the state along the Arabian Sea coast. ($1 = 35.8 rupees)
